topic: Threatened Species and Biodiversity in the Philippines
key_concepts: Biodiversity describes all living organisms within an ecosystem or habitat.
Extinction is the complete disappearance of a species from Earth.
Conservation status classifies species based on extinction risk.
Threatened species are likely to go extinct if not protected.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered species endemic to the Philippines.
High biodiversity ecosystems contain many species and have ecological advantages.
Low biodiversity ecosystems contain fewer species.
Extinction of a species reduces the biodiversity of an ecosystem.
A biome is a larger ecological unit than an ecosystem.
The aquatic biome includes ecosystems such as kelp forests, coral reefs, mangroves, estuar
Each aquatic ecosystem contributes to the biodiversity of its biome.
Damage to one ecosystem can compromise the entire biome.
